# ADI — Terms of Use

## How to read this document

This document contains two kinds of text, and they do not carry the same weight.

**Binding sections** are marked *binding*. They are written prose. They name no country, on
purpose: sanctions programmes change, and a clause that enumerates jurisdictions goes stale and
then states something untrue, while a clause that references the authority stays correct without
maintenance.

**Informational sections** are marked *informational*. They are generated from a dataset, they
carry the date that dataset was last reviewed, and they are a courtesy to the reader. They are not
operative. Where an informational section and a binding section disagree — because the list has
aged, or because an entry was misfiled — **the binding section governs.**

## 1. Where ADI is available — *binding*

ADI is not available in any jurisdiction or region subject to comprehensive sanctions administered
by the U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC), or in any
jurisdiction where provision of the software is otherwise prohibited.

This clause names no jurisdiction. It is written against the sanctions authority itself, so that it
remains accurate whether or not the list in the next section has kept up with it.

### Syria — comprehensive embargo

*Reviewed 2026-08-22 · open question.* No dealings of any kind.

### Russia — product category prohibited

*Reviewed 2026-08-22 · open question.* Not embargoed; the restriction attaches to software of this
kind.

Russia is not comprehensively embargoed. What is prohibited is a category of software, and whether
ADI — a task tree with roles and orchestration — sits inside that category is the open question, not
a settled exclusion.

Authorities:

- **OFAC** — [Determination under E.O. 14071 §1(a)(ii)](https://ofac.treasury.gov/sanctions-programs-and-country-information/russian-harmful-foreign-activities-sanctions), effective 2024-09-12 · FAQ 1187 names project management.
- **BIS** — [15 CFR 746.8(a)(8) — Sanctions against Russia and Belarus](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-15/section-746.8) · Names project management software, and explicitly its updates.
- **EU** — [Regulation (EU) 833/2014, Annex XXXIX](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2014/833/oj) · The same line item as the BIS section.

## 3. People, not only places — *binding*

Sanctions restrictions attach to persons as well as to places. A person or entity designated on
OFAC's Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons (SDN) List may not be dealt with in any
jurisdiction — including one where ADI is otherwise fully available and carries no territorial
restriction at all.

Counterparties are screened against that list before an enterprise sale.

## 4. Telemetry and where your data lives — *statement of fact*

This section states facts, not intentions. Each line was checked against the source tree on the
date given below. Where a line speaks about something ADI does not currently do, it is an
undertaking about how such a thing would be introduced if it ever were.

Verified on 2026-08-22 by reading the source tree of this repository:

- ADI contains no telemetry and no phone-home of any kind.
- If anything of that kind is ever added, its entire payload is documented before it ships.
- Anything of that kind has an obvious way to turn it off.
- Everything ADI holds lives in `~/.adi/mono`, on the machine you run it on.
